args.title: Invalid custom leaves current game unchanged
args.description: A refused Custom configuration shows a message and does not alter or abandon the current game.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in any status When the player submits a Custom configuration outside the limits Then a validation message is shown and the current game, its board, timer and counter remain unchanged

@dataclass
class Game:
    """Game.

    cells: the Cell records this Game owns, one dict each with the keys id (str), row (int), column (int), has_mine (bool), adjacent_mine_count (int), state (str).
    """
    id: str
    difficulty_id: str
    width: int
    height: int
    mine_count: int
    remaining_mines: int
    created_at: str
    status: str = "Ready"
    mines_laid: bool = True
    flags_placed: int = 0
    elapsed_seconds: int = 0
    started_at: Optional[str] = None
    ended_at: Optional[str] = None
    struck_cell_id: Optional[str] = None
    cells: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    events: List[Any] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith("_")
        }

kwargs.interface_contract:
- Action `open_cell`: params [`row`, `column`] — Opens the cell at zero-based (row, column), and is allowed only while status is Ready or Playing. On the first open of a Ready game, mines_laid becomes True and exactly mine_count mines are placed at random on cells other than the opened one. Every cell's adjacent_mine_count is then set to its mines among the existing up-to-8 neighbours, status becomes Playing and started_at is set. A Hidden safe cell becomes Opened; if its count is 0 the cascade opens Hidden neighbours, repeating through zeros, stopping at numbered cells and skipping Flagged cells. If the cell holds a mine it becomes Detonated, struck_cell_id holds its id, status becomes Lost, ended_at is set and elapsed_seconds freezes. When the last non-mine cell is opened, status becomes Won, ended_at is set, every mine cell is set to Flagged, flags_placed equals mine_count and remaining_mines is 0. Opening an Opened, Detonated or Flagged cell, or opening any cell in a Won, Lost or Abandoned game, changes nothing and raises no error.
- Action `toggle_flag`: params [`row`, `column`] — Switches a Hidden cell to Flagged (flags_placed +1) or a Flagged cell back to Hidden (flags_placed −1), and is allowed only while status is Ready or Playing. Afterwards remaining_mines = mine_count − flags_placed, which may go negative; flags are unlimited. Toggling an Opened or Detonated cell, or any cell in a Won, Lost or Abandoned game, changes nothing and raises no error.
- Action `chord_cell`: params [`row`, `column`] — Applies only to an Opened cell with adjacent_mine_count N ≥ 1 while status is Playing. If exactly N of its neighbours are Flagged, every Hidden neighbour is opened exactly as open_cell would, including cascades, a win, or a loss if a neighbour is a mine (that cell becomes Detonated, struck_cell_id is set and status becomes Lost). If the flag count differs from N, the cell is Hidden, Flagged or a zero cell, or the game is not Playing, nothing changes and no error is raised.
- Action `tick`: params [None] — The clock advancing one second: while status is Playing, elapsed_seconds increases by 1, capped at 999. In any other status nothing changes.
- Action `restart_game`: params [None] — Pressing the smiley. If status is Ready or Playing it becomes Abandoned and ended_at is set; if Won or Lost the outcome is kept. Returns a new Game with a new id and the same difficulty_id, width, height and mine_count, in its starting state.
- Action `change_difficulty`: params [`difficulty_id`, `width`, `height`, `mine_count`] — Choosing a difficulty from the menu: beginner gives 9×9 with 10 mines, intermediate 16×16 with 40, expert 30×16 with 99. Custom uses the given width (9–30), height (9–24) and mine_count (10 to (width−1)×(height−1)); out-of-range or unknown values raise InvalidConfigurationError and leave this game completely unchanged. When the choice is valid, a Ready or Playing game becomes Abandoned (Won or Lost keep their outcome), and a new Game with a new id and the chosen difficulty_id, width, height and mine_count is returned in its starting state.
- Action `abandon_game`: params [None] — Closing or leaving the game: if status is Ready or Playing it becomes Abandoned, ended_at is set and elapsed_seconds freezes. A Won, Lost or Abandoned game is left unchanged with no error; nothing is ever scored.
- A newly created `Game` (constructed with only its required fields) holds: Constructed with id, difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count, remaining_mines and created_at: status 'Ready', mines_laid False, flags_placed 0, elapsed_seconds 0, remaining_mines equal to mine_count, started_at, ended_at and struck_cell_id None, events empty. cells holds width×height dicts in row-major order, with zero-based row and column and id f"{row}-{column}" (e.g. '0-0'). Each cell has has_mine False, adjacent_mine_count 0 and state 'Hidden'.
- Field `status` holds exactly one of: "Ready" (New game, no cell opened yet, no mines laid, timer at 0); "Playing" (First cell opened; mines laid and timer running); "Won" (Every non-mine cell is opened; board locked); "Lost" (A mine was opened (directly or by a chord); board locked); "Abandoned" (Left from Ready or Playing via restart, difficulty change or closing; no score)
- Field `cells[].state` holds exactly one of: "Hidden" (Not opened and not flagged); "Flagged" (Marked by the player (or auto-flagged mine on a win); cannot be opened); "Opened" (Safe cell revealed, showing adjacent_mine_count); "Detonated" (The mine cell the player opened, causing the loss)
- Field `difficulty_id` holds exactly one of: "beginner" (9×9, 10 mines); "intermediate" (16×16, 40 mines); "expert" (30 wide × 16 high, 99 mines); "custom" (Player-chosen width 9–30, height 9–24, mines 10 to (width−1)×(height−1); no best time)
- A refusal raises `InvalidConfigurationError` when change_difficulty receives an unknown difficulty_id, or Custom width, height or mine_count outside the allowed limits; the message states the limits and the game is unchanged
- A refusal raises `CellNotFoundError` when open_cell, toggle_flag or chord_cell names a row or column outside the grid
- A refusal raises `InvalidTransitionError` when an internal status or cell-state change outside the allowed set is attempted. Allowed status changes are Ready→Playing, Playing→Won, Playing→Lost and Ready/Playing→Abandoned. Allowed cell changes are Hidden↔Flagged, Hidden→Opened and Hidden→Detonated. Ignored player actions never raise it.
kwargs.other_rules:
- Rectangular grid with fixed mine count: Given a game configured with width W, height H and mine count M When the mines are laid Then the board has exactly W×H cells and exactly M cells hold a mine
- Beginner preset: Given the player chooses Beginner When the new game is created Then its width is 9, height is 9 and mine count is 10
- Intermediate preset: Given the player chooses Intermediate When the new game is created Then its width is 16, height is 16 and mine count is 40
- Expert preset: Given the player chooses Expert When the new game is created Then its width is 30, height is 16 and mine count is 99
- Custom width range: Given the player enters a Custom configuration When the width is between 9 and 30 inclusive Then the width is accepted, and When the width is below 9 or above 30 Then the configuration is refused
- Custom height range: Given the player enters a Custom configuration When the height is between 9 and 24 inclusive Then the height is accepted, and When the height is below 9 or above 24 Then the configuration is refused
- Custom mine count range: Given a Custom configuration with valid width W and height H When the mine count is between 10 and (W−1)×(H−1) inclusive Then it is accepted, and When it is below 10 or above (W−1)×(H−1) Then the configuration is refused
- Mines laid on first open: Given a game in Ready status with no mines laid When the player opens the first cell Then the mines are laid at that moment, and before that moment no cell holds a mine
- First click is safe: Given a game in Ready status When the player opens any cell as the first open Then that cell holds no mine and the game does not end in a loss
- Ready to Playing transition: Given a game in Ready status When the player opens a hidden unflagged cell Then the game status becomes Playing
- Open a hidden unflagged cell: Given a game in Ready or Playing status and a cell in Hidden state When the player opens it Then the cell state becomes Opened (or Detonated if it holds a mine)
- Neighbour mine count: Given an interior safe cell with K mines among its 8 neighbours When it is opened Then its adjacent mine count is K (0 to 8)
- Edge and corner neighbours: Given a safe cell on an edge (5 neighbours) or a corner (3 neighbours) When its adjacent mine count is computed Then only the neighbours that exist within the grid are counted
- Cascade on zero: Given a hidden safe cell with adjacent mine count 0 When it is opened Then all its hidden neighbours are opened, and any opened neighbour with count 0 opens its neighbours in turn
- Cascade stops at numbered cells: Given a cascade in progress When it opens a cell with adjacent mine count of 1 or more Then that cell is opened and its own neighbours are not opened by the cascade
- Cascade skips flagged cells: Given a cascade in progress and a neighbouring cell in Flagged state When the cascade reaches it Then the cell remains Flagged and is not opened
- Toggle flag: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player flags a Hidden cell Then it becomes Flagged, and When the player flags a Flagged cell Then it becomes Hidden
- Flagged cell cannot be opened: Given a cell in Flagged state When the player tries to open it Then the cell stays Flagged and nothing is revealed, and When the player unflags it and opens it Then it is opened
- Unlimited flags: Given a game whose flags placed already equals its mine count When the player flags another Hidden cell Then the flag is placed
- Remaining mines counter: Given a game with M mines and F flags placed When the counter is calculated Then it equals M − F, including negative values when F > M
- Chord with matching flags: Given a game in Playing status and an Opened cell with number N and exactly N flagged neighbours When the player chords it Then all its Hidden unflagged neighbours are opened (with cascades as applicable)
- Chord with mismatched flags does nothing: Given an Opened cell with number N and a number of flagged neighbours different from N When the player chords it Then no cell changes state
- Chord with wrong flag loses: Given an Opened cell with number N and N flagged neighbours, one of which is not a mine When the player chords it Then the unflagged mine neighbour is opened, becomes Detonated and the game status becomes Lost
- Timer starts at first open: Given a game in Ready status with elapsed seconds 0 When the player opens the first cell Then the timer starts and elapsed seconds increases by 1 each second
- Timer cap at 999: Given a game in Playing status with elapsed seconds 999 When further time passes Then elapsed seconds stays at 999
- Timer freezes on end: Given a game in Playing status When the game becomes Won or Lost Then elapsed seconds is frozen at its current value
- Opening a mine loses: Given a game in Playing status When the player opens a Hidden cell holding a mine Then the cell becomes Detonated, it is recorded as the struck cell and the game status becomes Lost
- Win condition: Given a game in Playing status When the last non-mine cell is opened Then the game status becomes Won whether or not the mines are flagged, and while any non-mine cell is unopened the game is not Won
- Auto-flag on win: Given a game that has just become Won When the win is recorded Then every mine cell is set to Flagged, flags placed equals the mine count and the remaining-mines counter is 0
- Board lock after end: Given a game in Won or Lost status When the player opens, flags or chords any cell Then no cell, counter or timer changes, and When the player starts a new game Then it is accepted
- Opening an opened cell is ignored: Given a cell in Opened state When the player opens it Then nothing changes and no message is shown
- Flagging an opened cell is ignored: Given a cell in Opened state When the player toggles a flag on it Then the cell stays Opened, flags placed is unchanged and no message is shown
- Chording a hidden cell is ignored: Given a cell in Hidden state When the player chords it Then no cell changes state and no message is shown
- Restart via smiley: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player presses the smiley Then that game becomes Abandoned with no best time recorded and a new Ready game of the same difficulty with all cells Hidden, timer 0 and counter equal to its mine count is created
- Smiley after end starts new game: Given a game in Won or Lost status When the player presses the smiley Then the finished game keeps its outcome and a new Ready game of the same difficulty is created
- Changing difficulty: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player chooses a valid difficulty Then the current game becomes Abandoned with no score and a new Ready game with the chosen width, height and mine count is created
- Leaving abandons the game: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player closes the game Then it becomes Abandoned and no best time is recorded
- Abandon only from Ready or Playing: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When it is abandoned Then its status becomes Abandoned, and Given a game in Won or Lost status When an abandon is triggered Then its status remains Won or Lost
- Game status transitions: Given a game in any status When a transition is requested Then only Ready→Playing, Playing→Won, Playing→Lost and Ready or Playing→Abandoned are allowed and all other transitions are refused
- Cell state transitions: Given a cell When its state changes Then only Hidden↔Flagged, Hidden→Opened (safe) and Hidden→Detonated (mine) are allowed, and an Opened or Detonated cell never returns to Hidden or Flagged

import copy

import pytest

from src.domain.game import Game


WIDTH = 9
HEIGHT = 9
MINES = 10
# Mines along the whole top row plus the first cell of the second row: 10 mines.
MINE_POSITIONS = {(0, c) for c in range(9)} | {(1, 0)}


def _adjacent(row, column):
    count = 0
    for dr in (-1, 0, 1):
        for dc in (-1, 0, 1):
            if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                continue
            r, c = row + dr, column + dc
            if 0 <= r < HEIGHT and 0 <= c < WIDTH and (r, c) in MINE_POSITIONS:
                count += 1
    return count


def _fresh_cells():
    return [
        {
            "id": f"{r}-{c}",
            "row": r,
            "column": c,
            "has_mine": False,
            "adjacent_mine_count": 0,
            "state": "Hidden",
        }
        for r in range(HEIGHT)
        for c in range(WIDTH)
    ]


def _mined_cells():
    cells = _fresh_cells()
    for cell in cells:
        pos = (cell["row"], cell["column"])
        cell["has_mine"] = pos in MINE_POSITIONS
        cell["adjacent_mine_count"] = _adjacent(*pos)
    return cells


def _cell(cells, row, column):
    return cells[row * WIDTH + column]


def _game_in(status):
    game = Game(
        id="g1",
        difficulty_id="beginner",
        width=WIDTH,
        height=HEIGHT,
        mine_count=MINES,
        remaining_mines=MINES,
        created_at="2024-01-01T10:00:00Z",
    )
    game.events = []
    if status == "Ready":
        game.status = "Ready"
        game.mines_laid = False
        game.flags_placed = 0
        game.remaining_mines = MINES
        game.elapsed_seconds = 0
        game.started_at = None
        game.ended_at = None
        game.struck_cell_id = None
        game.cells = _fresh_cells()
    elif status == "Playing":
        game.status = "Playing"
        game.mines_laid = True
        cells = _mined_cells()
        _cell(cells, 8, 8)["state"] = "Opened"
        _cell(cells, 0, 0)["state"] = "Flagged"
        game.cells = cells
        game.flags_placed = 1
        game.remaining_mines = MINES - 1
        game.elapsed_seconds = 42
        game.started_at = "2024-01-01T10:01:00Z"
        game.ended_at = None
        game.struck_cell_id = None
    elif status == "Lost":
        game.status = "Lost"
        game.mines_laid = True
        cells = _mined_cells()
        _cell(cells, 8, 8)["state"] = "Opened"
        _cell(cells, 0, 1)["state"] = "Detonated"
        game.cells = cells
        game.flags_placed = 0
        game.remaining_mines = MINES
        game.elapsed_seconds = 17
        game.started_at = "2024-01-01T10:01:00Z"
        game.ended_at = "2024-01-01T10:01:17Z"
        game.struck_cell_id = "0-1"
    elif status == "Won":
        game.status = "Won"
        game.mines_laid = True
        cells = _mined_cells()
        for cell in cells:
            cell["state"] = "Flagged" if cell["has_mine"] else "Opened"
        game.cells = cells
        game.flags_placed = MINES
        game.remaining_mines = 0
        game.elapsed_seconds = 88
        game.started_at = "2024-01-01T10:01:00Z"
        game.ended_at = "2024-01-01T10:02:28Z"
        game.struck_cell_id = None
    elif status == "Abandoned":
        game.status = "Abandoned"
        game.mines_laid = True
        cells = _mined_cells()
        _cell(cells, 8, 8)["state"] = "Opened"
        _cell(cells, 0, 0)["state"] = "Flagged"
        game.cells = cells
        game.flags_placed = 1
        game.remaining_mines = MINES - 1
        game.elapsed_seconds = 30
        game.started_at = "2024-01-01T10:01:00Z"
        game.ended_at = "2024-01-01T10:01:30Z"
        game.struck_cell_id = None
    return game


def _snapshot(game):
    return copy.deepcopy(
        {
            "id": game.id,
            "difficulty_id": game.difficulty_id,
            "width": game.width,
            "height": game.height,
            "mine_count": game.mine_count,
            "remaining_mines": game.remaining_mines,
            "created_at": game.created_at,
            "status": game.status,
            "mines_laid": game.mines_laid,
            "flags_placed": game.flags_placed,
            "elapsed_seconds": game.elapsed_seconds,
            "started_at": game.started_at,
            "ended_at": game.ended_at,
            "struck_cell_id": game.struck_cell_id,
            "cells": game.cells,
            "events": game.events,
        }
    )


# Each refused configuration is paired below with an accepted one differing only
# in the single value that crosses the limit.
REFUSED = [
    pytest.param(8, 9, 10, id="width-below-9"),
    pytest.param(31, 9, 10, id="width-above-30"),
    pytest.param(9, 8, 10, id="height-below-9"),
    pytest.param(9, 25, 10, id="height-above-24"),
    pytest.param(9, 9, 9, id="mines-below-10"),
    pytest.param(9, 9, 65, id="mines-above-(9-1)x(9-1)=64"),
]

ACCEPTED = [
    pytest.param(9, 9, 10, id="width-exactly-9"),
    pytest.param(30, 9, 10, id="width-exactly-30"),
    pytest.param(9, 9, 10, id="height-exactly-9"),
    pytest.param(9, 24, 10, id="height-exactly-24"),
    pytest.param(9, 9, 10, id="mines-exactly-10"),
    pytest.param(9, 9, 64, id="mines-exactly-64"),
]

STATUSES = ["Ready", "Playing", "Won", "Lost", "Abandoned"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("status", STATUSES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("width,height,mine_count", REFUSED)
def test_invalid_custom_is_refused_and_leaves_game_unchanged(
    status, width, height, mine_count
):
    game = _game_in(status)
    before = _snapshot(game)

    with pytest.raises(Exception) as exc_info:
        game.change_difficulty(
            difficulty_id="custom",
            width=width,
            height=height,
            mine_count=mine_count,
        )

    # The value lies outside width 9–30, height 9–24 or mines 10–(W−1)×(H−1),
    # so the configuration is refused with InvalidConfigurationError.
    assert type(exc_info.value).__name__ == "InvalidConfigurationError"
    # A validation message is shown to the player: it is not empty.
    assert str(exc_info.value).strip() != ""

    # A refused configuration does not alter or abandon the game: status,
    # every cell (state, mine, count), timer, flags and counter are exactly
    # as they were before the call.
    after = _snapshot(game)
    assert after["status"] == status
    assert after["cells"] == before["cells"]
    assert after["elapsed_seconds"] == before["elapsed_seconds"]
    assert after["remaining_mines"] == before["remaining_mines"]
    assert after["flags_placed"] == before["flags_placed"]
    assert after == before


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width,height,mine_count", ACCEPTED)
def test_custom_exactly_at_limits_is_accepted(width, height, mine_count):
    game = _game_in("Ready")

    new_game = game.change_difficulty(
        difficulty_id="custom",
        width=width,
        height=height,
        mine_count=mine_count,
    )

    # Every value is within its inclusive limits, so no error is raised and a
    # new game with the chosen configuration is returned in its starting state.
    assert new_game.id != game.id
    assert new_game.difficulty_id == "custom"
    assert new_game.width == width
    assert new_game.height == height
    assert new_game.mine_count == mine_count
    assert new_game.status == "Ready"
    assert new_game.elapsed_seconds == 0
    assert new_game.flags_placed == 0
    assert new_game.remaining_mines == mine_count
    assert len(new_game.cells) == width * height
    assert all(cell["state"] == "Hidden" for cell in new_game.cells)
    # The valid choice abandons the previous Ready game.
    assert game.status == "Abandoned"
